title: Apples Over the Hedge

lines.cy: Ti sy nesa, John? Ti'n barod i weud wrth y fainc am yr afale?
lines.en: You're next, John? Ready to tell the bench about the apples?
lines.es: ¿Sos el próximo, John? ¿Estás listo para contarle al juez lo de las manzanas?

shots.direction: Reverse angle. John, cap in his hands and Sunday coat buttoned, answers Gwen in a low voice. She sits just off camera to his left. Medium close on John only. About 16 seconds.

lines.accent: thick Glamorgan Welsh, whispered (Welsh marked for native review)
lines.cy: Odw, glei. Ond yn Saesneg fydd e, cofia, a'r Saesneg yn sownd yn 'y ngheg i. Perllan 'Nhad, dros y clawdd o'r rheilffordd. 'Na i gyd sy gen i i weud.
lines.en: I am, aye. But it'll be in English, mind, and the English sticks in my mouth. Father's orchard, over the hedge from the railway. That's all I've got to tell.
lines.es: Sí, che. Pero va a ser en inglés, ojo, y el inglés se me traba en la boca. El huerto de mi padre, por encima del seto desde el ferrocarril. Es todo lo que tengo para decir.

shots.direction: Wide still of the court in session. The usher stands by the door in a dark uniform coat. A man sits in the dock, seen only from behind in a corduroy jacket. His face is never shown. lines.cy: John Williams yr ieuengaf. Dywedwch wrth y fainc: perllan pwy yw hi, a ble mae'r clawdd 'ma'n sefyll?
lines.en: John Williams junior. Tell the bench: whose orchard is it, and where does this hedge stand?
lines.es: John Williams hijo. Dígale al tribunal: ¿de quién es el huerto, y dónde está ese seto?

shots.direction: John in the witness box, both hands on the wooden rail, looking up at the magistrate just off camera above him. He speaks carefully in English with a thick Glamorgan accent. Medium close on John only. About 15 seconds.
shots.image_prompt: photoreal 16:9 still, 1889 Victorian police court witness box, a Welsh farmer's son in his twenties with a lean sunburnt face, light brown short hair, a thin moustache and pale blue eyes, in a dark wool Sunday coat and waistcoat, both hands gripping a varnished wooden rail, looking upward at someone out of frame, panelled wall behind, soft window light, invented face, no text, no heraldry

lines.accent: thick Glamorgan Welsh accent, speaking English carefully
lines.cy: Perllan Fferm y Tŷ Mawr yw hi, syr, lan yn Llandochau. Eiddo John Williams, 'y nhad i, 'na fe. Ma'r clawdd yn rhedeg ar hyd y rheilffordd, chweld, a'r afale wedi'u cyrraedd dros y clawdd o'r lein.
lines.en: It's the orchard of Great House Farm, sir, up at Llandough. The property of John Williams, my father, that is. The hedge do run along the railway, see, and the apples was reached over from the line.
lines.es: Es el huerto de Great House Farm, señor, allá arriba en Llandough. Propiedad de John Williams, mi padre, digamos. El seto corre a lo largo del ferrocarril, ¿vio?, y las manzanas las alcanzaron por encima desde la vía.

shots.direction: Still of the place John describes. A hawthorn hedge tops the railway embankment below the hill at Llandough. Apple trees heavy with August fruit lean over it, and the iron rails run below toward Penarth. A thin drift of lime-kiln smoke rises from the far hillside. No people and no train. Slow push along the hedge line. Ambience: wasps, wind in leaves, a distant train whistle. About 20 seconds.

Inferred: that the hearing was at the Penarth police court, the exact day (between 11 and 16 August 1889), the magistrate's wording, and the Welsh whispered exchanges. Gwen is invented. The accused is not named and the outcome is not shown.
